text:
ajay: Heads up — found a case where retries + routing to fallback model are leading to double token credits when streams are truncated. Repro steps attached.

maria: ugh, seen that before with partial-stream ACKs. what's the triggering sequence?

ajay: sequence: client starts streaming request -> server streams tokens -> router times out and issues retry to fallback (different node/model) -> both streams write usage events before the original is cancelled -> client receives final truncated chunk from fallback and a cancel on the old stream.

ajay: example logs (simplified):
```
2026-03-04T12:01:05Z request_id=R1 route=us-east-1 model=mpt-10b node=A status=streaming tokens_emitted=42
2026-03-04T12:01:06Z retry_id=R1-r1 route=us-west-2 model=mpt-7b node=B status=streaming tokens_emitted=58
2026-03-04T12:01:06Z request_id=R1 status=cancelled reason=router_retry
2026-03-04T12:01:07Z retry_id=R1-r1 status=complete tokens_total=58
2026-03-04T12:01:07Z usage_event request_ref=R1 tokens=42
2026-03-04T12:01:07Z usage_event request_ref=R1-r1 tokens=58
```
```
# client sees 58 tokens, billing shows 100 total credited
```

kevin: that matches an earlier incident but here it's trickier because the router issues the retry rather than the client. Currently accounting is per-stream commit event, and both streams commit.

maria: suggested quick mitigation last time: only emit usage_event for the stream that ends with a final "complete" status AND that has the latest sequence nonce. But router-driven retries can interleave completions and cancels in weird orders.

diane: open question: should we 1) dedupe on request_id parent (attribute to original parent), 2) dedupe on client-visible idempotency token, or 3) only credit the lowest-cost successful model? Each has tradeoffs.

ajay: pros/cons:
- parent dedupe: easy if router preserves parent id across internal retries. But we don't always have parent id for older clients.
- idempotency token: ideal but requires SDK change and won't help 3rd party clients.
- lowest-cost heuristic: risky, could under-credit if fallback actually did more work (e.g., longer contexts).

kevin: console UX ask: we should show both emitted credits and "final billed" credits in per-request trace, and highlight retries. That will help customers debug but doesn't solve internal correctness.

maria: telemetry idea: add retry_id and parent_id tags to all usage events, plus a finalization flag. Then accounting job can collapse events by parent_id preferring the event with finalization=true. If no finalization, fall back to latest event timestamp.

ajay: potential race: both streams might set finalization=true if router races. We could make finalization a compare-and-swap on a centralized request record (in Redis) that stores finalizer=retry_id. First writer wins, others become non-final. But that adds latency and a new hot key per request.

kevin: on the cost side, adding a CAS in the hot path could add ~1-2ms P50 which might matter for low-latency plans. But P99 remains dominated by model. We should gate CAS behind a config flag enabled for enterprise accounts first.

maria: another option: emit provisional usage events for streaming frames (to drive observability) but delay billing-ingestion until a confirmed terminal event. We already buffer per-request in billing pipeline for 30s for similar reasons. Could extend to hold provisional events and only materialize final invoice rows after collapse. Downside: reporting lag and increased pipeline memory.

ajay: minimal change that fixes correctness: make router attach "parent_request" to any internal retry and ensure the node that performs the final write to the usage store includes the parent_request and a terminal boolean. Then run a nightly reconciliation for duplicates within a 24h window. But reconciliation is messy and impacts chargeback immediacy.

diane: thinking about policy: what should the default from a product standpoint be? Immediate but possibly slightly over-count when router retried vs always exact with a small lag. Legal/compliance folks prefer exact, sales prefer immediate.

kevin: product suggestion: different account tiers. Free/dev accounts accept fast but eventual reconciliation; enterprise has exactness SLA with finalization CAS enabled and console shows pending vs confirmed credits.

maria: implementation notes:
- add fields to usage_event: parent_id, retry_id, terminal=true|false, model_variant, route_hint
- router must propagate parent_id and set retry_id when spawning an internal retry
- streaming nodes should not write a terminal=true usage_event until they know they're the finalizer (either by CAS or by being the only stream left)

ajay: sample usage_event JSON we could emit from runtime (single-line in logs for readability):
```
{"ts":"2026-03-04T12:01:07Z","event_type":"usage","request_id":"R1-r1","parent_id":"R1","retry_id":"R1-r1","tokens":58,"terminal":true,"model":"mpt-7b","node":"B"}
```

maria: +1. We also need to update console to present "provisional" tokens in yellow and final tokens in green, and an explanation tooltip.

kevin: ops: how painful is enabling CAS per-request? infra-bot, can you estimate?

infra-bot: quick estimate: adding a single Redis key per request with GET/SETNX/GET adds ~0.5-3ms depending on region and topology. We can shard by request_id prefix to reduce hotkey collisions. Storage overhead negligible. Estimated work: 2-3 sprint days infra + 1-2 runtime days to integrate and feature-flag.

maria: thanks. Another corner: tool calls. If model calls a tool and tool issues its own usage (webhook or external compute), those tokens should be considered part of the same parent trace. Router retries could cause the tool to be invoked twice. We need idempotency tokens for tool calls too.

ajay: agree — tool-call idempotency is crucial. Propose adding tool_call_id generated by runtime and passed to tool invocations; tools should dedupe by that id. Also add to usage_event so we can attribute tool compute tokens to the originating request.

diane: can we get a short RFC and a migration plan? Key pieces: telemetry schema change, router propagation, runtime CAS (feature-flagged), console UI changes, billing pipeline hold window extension, tool-call idempotency.

ajay: I'll draft RFC. Owners: ajay (runtime), maria (billing/console), kevin (product), diane (policy). Aim for RFC in one week.

maria: one more UX ask: expose a per-request "billing lineage" JSON in the console that shows all usage_event rows and which one won finalization. That will make audits trivial.

kevin: agree. And add a metric that reports percent of requests with duplicate provisional credit events — we want to track whether mitigation reduced duplicates.

diane: ok sounds like a plan. If anyone has objections to the CAS finalizer approach, raise now. Otherwise I'll add policy notes about staggered rollout and feature flags for enterprise-only.

kevin: no objections from me.

ajay: no objections. I'll start the RFC with the example logs and proposed schema.

maria: thanks — filing a console ticket to add provisional/final display states and the lineage view. :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Created billing ticket #BI-4219 for "dedupe billing for router retries" assigned to maria, severity=high

ajay: pinging next week for RFC review.

maria: thanks, closing loop.
